body:
Merged main to resolve conflicts (crates/ui/src/egui_app/mod.rs: keep both sides). Each side added one module line: `sim_steps` from this PR and `ribbon_cell` from #2755. The diff against main lists only the files of this PR.

Targeted gate on the merge:
- `camcraft-ui` lib, `sim_op_steps` and `ribbon` filters: 40 passed.
- `camcraft-sim` `sim_op_steps`: 6 passed.
- `camcraft-app` `sim_op_step_stock`: 2 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Ready for a re-check (/resolve-conflicts check).

<!-- pr-reviewer: ed4773c6784f72471259a315631fcf75cc8cdac7 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** There are two small items. The behaviour is correct, and each suite is green.

This is not a SAFETY-tier review. The PR adds lookups on `sim::Script` and two buttons. It does not change posted G-code, a gouge or collision check, the stock simulation or geometry.

## What looks good

- The lookup is in `camcraft-sim` (`crates/sim/src/sim_steps.rs`), so the stand-alone simulator (#2587) can use it. The UI part is one call in `shell.rs`.
- The playhead is view state, so no command and no MCP tool are necessary. The body says so.
- A non-finite playhead, an empty script and an operation with no moves have tests. The new source has no `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!`.
- `sim_op_step_stock` compares the stock after a step with the stock of playback move by move, across a tool change.
- The body has the before and after screenshots, the `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #2608`. The decision record is in `docs/decisions/2608-sim-op-step.md`.
- The tips use the same `\t<key>` form as the tips in `panes.rs`.

## Results merged with main (locally, macOS arm64)

Trial merge of `ed4773c67` with `upstream/main` at `9ff2dda25`: clean, 11 files.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-sim` lib | 192 passed |
| `camcraft-sim` `sim_op_steps` | 6 passed |
| `camcraft-app` `sim_op_step_stock` | 2 passed |
| `camcraft-ui` lib (CWD `crates/ui`) | 1259 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored |
| `camcraft-ui` `boundary`, `boundary_picks`, `sinker_setup`, `tap_hand`, `theme_example`, `theme_files`, `waterjet_tool` | each green |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The first run was on main at `971c23faa`. There the four frame-cost tests of #2762 failed, as the body says. Main at `9ff2dda25` has the fix (#2767), and the `ui` lib suite is green on that merge.

**Extra suites run:** none. The diff changes no file under `testdata/` or a golden directory, and it does not touch the import code.

**Mutations (2):**

| Mutation in `crates/sim/src/sim_steps.rs` | Result |
|---|---|
| `prev_op_start`: `s < t - SAME_T` to `s <= t` | red: `previous_goes_to_the_current_start_then_to_the_one_before`, `the_first_and_the_last_operation_have_no_step_past_them` |
| `op_starts`: `self.cum.get(i - 1)` to `self.cum.get(i)` (the start moves to the end of the first segment of the operation) | **green**: `sim_op_steps` 6 passed, `sim_op_step_stock` 2 passed |

## Requested before merge

1. **`crates/ui/src/egui_app/sim_steps.rs:45-57` and `crates/sim/src/sim_steps.rs:27-63`: the steps walk each segment four times in each frame.** `op_step_buttons` calls `prev_op_start`, `next_op_start` and `op_starting_at` two times. Each call runs `op_starts()`, which reads all of `Script::segs`. The transport bar draws in each frame while the simulation is open, also when the playback is paused. Until now the transport cost was `Script::at` (a binary search) on the cached script.
   Measured with a scratch test (10 operations, 1 000 009 segments, the `MAX_SIM_SEGS` size): 14.7 ms for one frame in release, 66 ms in debug. At 100 000 segments this is about 1.5 ms in release.
   Fix: calculate the starts one time for each script. For example, fill a `Vec<(usize, f64)>` field when `sim::script` builds the `Script`, or keep the result beside `cached_script`. Then `next_op_start` and `prev_op_start` read that short list.

2. **`crates/sim/tests/sim_op_steps.rs:44-54`: no test pins the value of a start.** The second mutation above stays green. The tests compare the steps only with `op_starts()` itself, and `sc.at(s).op` is the same for each position in the operation. Add an assert of the value from the script: the start of operation 2 equals `sc.cum[k]`, where `k` is the last segment of operation 1 (and `sc.at(start - 1e-6).op` is the operation before).

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- Item 6 of #2608 asks for the keys "in the shortcut help". The decision record says that the app has no shortcut list and that the tips name the keys. This agrees with the other tips. The maintainer can decide if #2608 needs more.
- `crates/app/tests/sim_op_step_stock.rs:10-12`: the Gate map names `app::sim (Script::next_op_start, prev_op_start)`. `Script` is defined in `camcraft_sim::sim`. The law asks for the name of the owning crate.
- The keys are read while a dialog or a different window is open above the viewport, if no widget has the focus. I did not find a second user of Page Up or Page Down in `crates/`, so there is no conflict now.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs` is 1114 lines (1112 on main). It was above 400 before this PR.
- I did not open the two screenshots. I confirmed only that the body has a before image and an after image.
- The compile cache (sccache) did not answer on this machine, so the builds ran without it. This does not change a result.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Back to draft for the review fixes of the review on ed4773c67: the operation starts are calculated one time for each script, and a new test pins the value of a start. The Gate map line of `sim_op_step_stock.rs` gets the name of the owning crate.

Review fixes for the review on ed4773c67. New head: 235201581.

## 1. The starts are walked one time for each timeline

- `crates/sim/src/sim_steps.rs`: a new value type `OpStarts` (re-exported as `camcraft_sim::sim::OpStarts`). `OpStarts::of(&Script)` walks the segments one time. `next`, `prev` and `op_at` are binary searches (`partition_point`) over one entry for each operation. The `Script` methods stay for a one-time question; they call `OpStarts`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/sim_steps.rs`: `cached_op_starts(state)` keeps the starts in `State::sim_op_starts`, beside `sim_script_cache`. The key is the script's `Arc`, held as a `Weak`: a still frame gives the kept starts, a new timeline is walked one time, and the old script is freed. `op_step_buttons` takes `&OpStarts` and reads no segment.
- I did not put a starts field in `Script`. `Script` has public fields and tests build it field by field, so such a field can disagree with the segments. I did not keep the cache in egui memory: the frame-cost rule in `crates/ui/AGENTS.md` says that no widget holds a cache. The decision record has the two items.
- Pinned by `egui_app::tests::sim_op_steps::the_starts_are_walked_once_per_timeline`: still frames give the same `Arc` (no new walk); a document change gives new starts that equal a fresh `OpStarts::of`; the old script is freed.

## 2. A test pins the value of a start

- `crates/sim/tests/sim_op_steps.rs::each_start_is_the_end_of_the_last_segment_of_the_operation_before`: for each operation after the first, the start equals `sc.cum[k]`, where `k` is the last segment of the operation before. Segment `k + 1` opens the operation, and `sc.at(start - 1e-6).op` is the operation before.
- Your second mutation (`self.cum.get(i - 1)` to `get(i)`) is now red: this test fails at line 116.
- `kept_starts_answer_as_the_script_lookups` compares `OpStarts` with the `Script` lookups at each start, on each side of it, and at the ends (NaN and infinity included).

## Notes

- The Gate map line of `sim_op_step_stock.rs` now names `camcraft_sim::sim`.
- The branch has a merge of main (no conflicts). It brings the #2767 fix of #2762.

## Readings

- Quick gate on c3efcfe7c (before the merge of main): 25 of 26 steps ok. `ui suites: lib` failed only in the four #2762 tests.
- After the merge of main (235201581): `camcraft-ui` lib 1267 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored; `camcraft-sim` `sim_op_steps` 8 passed; `camcraft-app` `sim_op_step_stock` 2 passed; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Ready for a re-review.
